test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 23 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

When they left for Mexico, their house was in __good__ condition than it is now.
solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. better .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence compares the condition of the house in two different time periods — when they left for Mexico and its current state.
 
• In such comparisons, the correct word to use is the comparative form of "good," which is **"better."**
 
• Using other options like "more good," "excellent," or "best" is grammatically incorrect or contextually inappropriate in this case.

Correct sentence: *When they left for Mexico, their house was in **better** condition than it is now*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative adjectives:**

 
 
• Used to compare two things, e.g., "better," "worse," "taller," etc.
 
• Formed by adding "-er" to short adjectives or by using "more" with longer adjectives.
 
• **Example:** This book is **better** than that one.
 
 
 
• **Superlative adjectives:**

 
 
• Used to show the highest degree of comparison among three or more things, e.g., "best," "worst," "tallest," etc.
 
• Formed by adding "-est" to short adjectives or by using "most" with longer adjectives.
 
• **Example:** This is the **best** book in the library.
